RFC 4659 Section 3.2.1.1: "When the IPv6 VPN traffic is to be transported to the BGP speaker using IPv6 tunneling (e.g., IPv6 MPLS LSPs, IPsec-protected IPv6 tunnels), the BGP speaker SHALL advertise a Next Hop Network Address field containing a VPN-IPv6 address - whose 8-octet RD is set to zero, and - whose 16-octet IPv6 address is set to the global IPv6 address of the advertising BGP speaker." The moved unit is TestRFC4659LinkLocalPeeringPreservesUnspecifiedGlobalPair: it now calls advertiseFirst with the same body before receipt on both the cached and rs rails. Its positive assertion is unchanged: the link-local-only VPN case must reach the recipient as exactly one UPDATE with the exact 48-octet zero-RD/unspecified-global/zero-RD/link-local MP_REACH; the forbidden cases still require the exact MP_UNREACH (with the RFC 8277 0x800000 compatibility label for VPN) and no MP_REACH. The prior adj-out record does not suppress the valid re-announcement (asserted). This carrier remains contextual exception evidence for the Section 3.2.1.1 link-local peering sentence; the principal sender-identity proof stays TestRFC4659ConfiguredIPv6TransportNextHopWire (configured origination over TCP6, self and explicit selection, both grouping modes, exact zero RD and speaker-owned global), byte-identical, with TestUpdateBuilder_BuildVPN_IPv6_NextHop as encoding control. The {single-polarity: positive} annotation stays correct: a conditional sender-emission obligation, not receiver rejection.
